items.title: Willie Hightower Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: Yeah, well, we come along and me and Joe Oliver came along and he worked across the street from me.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, we come along and me and Joe Oliver came along and he worked across the street from me. I went to Tommel of France No. 6 School. Tommel of France No. 6. I forget the name of the school that Joe went to. But every evening we would play with one another with the hoes. His madam would holler at him and my madam would holler at me. But we had to just pump the street, pose across the street at one another. And we were both in short pants at that time. I was going on 10 years old, around 10. And after we…
What was your first instrument? Did you start on the cornet?

items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: me and Joe turned out to be the best friend, and when he got sick here on his last laps, I held his job down at the plantation for him for about six months

ctx.x: Would you like Keppert better than Joe Oliver?

Well, it's just like one of those things that, that I figured that although that me and Joe turned out to be the best friend, and when he got sick here on his last laps, I held his job down at the plantation for him for about six months, and did my work too, because he was unable to work. You see, he had a drummer in there by the name of, this drummer, went back in the orange. Oh, Paul Barber.
Paul Barber. Yeah, I know. He was racing one day. I'm a good friend of mine.
